# Fry Station Quick Reference (Grill)

Owner: Priya Nair, Sous Chef – Grill

## Station Scope & Setup
- You run all deep-fried items for Grill during service; keep fryers clean, hot, and safe.
- Two vats: left for proteins (chicken, fish), right for starch/veg (fries, rings, tots).
- Oil: canola blend. Keep backup jugs nearby, capped. Skimmer, spider, clean baskets ready.
- Thermometer and timer at hand; check internal temps on proteins.

## Oil Temps, Loads, and Targets
| Product | Set Oil Temp (°F) | Basket Load | Typical Fry Time | Target/Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Fries, 3/8 in | 350 | 1 lb per basket | 3–4 min | Golden, crisp; season immediately |
| Tater tots | 350 | 1 lb | 3–4 min | Crisp exterior |
| Onion rings | 350 | 12 oz | 2–3 min | Light golden, not greasy |
| Chicken tenders | 325 | 1 lb | 5–6 min | 165°F internal for 15 sec |
| Bone-in wings | 350 | 1 lb | 8–10 min | 165°F internal; rest 1 min |
| Fish fillet | 350 | 10–12 oz total | 3–5 min | 145°F internal for 15 sec |
| Hushpuppies | 350 | 12 oz | 3–4 min | Cook through, no gumminess |

## Basket Loading & Drop Procedure
1. Preheat to set temp; confirm with thermometer after recovery.
2. Pat wet items dry; dust proteins lightly in seasoned flour to reduce blow-off.
3. Load basket to listed max; shake to level. Do not overload—oil must cover freely.
4. Lower basket slowly to avoid boil-over; start timer.
5. Gently shake at 30 sec to break clumps; skim loose crumbs from vat surface.
6. Pull when color/texture hit; verify internal temps on proteins; hang 10–15 sec to drain.
7. Season starches immediately over drip pan; never over the vat.

## Oil Quality Checks (each hour and after rush)
- Color: pale gold to light amber is good; dark brown/black means change.
- Smoke: oil should not smoke at set temp; smoking = degraded or too hot.
- Foaming: persistent foam after drops = contamination; filter or change.
- Odor/Flavor: rancid, fishy, or burnt notes = change.
- Crumb load: heavy sediment on floor of vat = filter now.

## Filtering & Top-Off Basics
1. Set fryer to filter mode or power off; allow to cool to safe filter temp per unit label.
2. Skim surface; open drain slowly into filter pan with screen and paper/powder.
3. Scrape carbon from walls/heating elements with fryer brush; no water in vat.
4. Pump filtered oil back; strain a second time if still dark.
5. Top off with fresh oil to fill line; bring back to temp and test with a fry.

## When to Change Oil (Do Not Try to “Save” It)
- Oil smokes at proper set temps after filtering.
- Color is coffee-dark; flavors transfer between items.
- Foaming persists and recovery time is slow.
- After heavy fish/protein night if odor lingers post-filter.

## Burn Prevention & PPE
- Wear dry, long sleeves; use cut/heat gloves for basket moves and cleaning.
- Never drop wet or icy product; always shake off ice/water in a separate bin.
- Keep handles dry and pointed inward; don’t rest baskets over active vats.
- Walk, don’t run; announce “behind,” “hot,” “corner.”
- Salt/season away from vats to prevent popping and corrosion.

## Grease Fire Response
1. Do not use water. Do not move the fryer.
2. Turn off gas/power. Close fryer lid if safe.
3. Use K-class extinguisher: pull pin, aim at base, squeeze, sweep.
4. Call “Fire at Fryer,” clear guests/FOH line of sight, alert manager.
5. After discharge, do not relight. Wait for chef/maintenance review.

## End-of-Shift Reset & Log
1. Skim vats, filter if crumb load is moderate+, top off to line.
2. Wipe exterior, floors, and underframes; empty crumb trays.
3. Thermometer sanitized; timers cleared; tools washed/air-dried.
4. Record filter/change in fryer log with initials and notes (color, smell, actions).
summary: Fry station quick reference for Hearthline: temps, loads, oil care, filtering, safety, and fire response for new line cooks.
